**Note: this post contains AI-generated content.** The CAD design, the STEP file, and the derivations below were generated by ChatGPT Astra, not designed by me.

I am exploring the new ChatGPT Astra. I wanted to see how good it is at design.

### Prompt

I want you to design a quasi-direct-drive actuator for a legged robotics application (quadruped). Here are the necessary requirements, which you cannot break:

You have to use the CubeMars RO100 frameless motor. As this does not have a frame for the rotor, you have the flexibility to design it as per the requirement.
The gearbox should be present inside the motor, where there is plenty of space in its inner core.
The gear ratio should be 8:1.
You are absolutely allowed to take many references from research papers, other actuator designs, and company catalogs.
Each and every design choice should be objective, based on physics and mechanical engineering theorems and proofs (e.g., the number of bolts and their size based on shear stress and load-carrying capacity, bearing selection based on static and dynamic capacities, gear design based on the Lewis equation, and material selection based on yield strength and thermal properties).
You can use cross-platform solutions for the design, like using fins for cooling and heat pipes for removing heat.

At the end:

I want you to give me the design in a STEP file with multiple parts in it.
I also want the complete theoretical derivation and explanation of why you did what you did. You are free to include diagrams as well. Just give it to me in any reasonable format.

Design it generated, viewable right here in the browser (drag to orbit, scroll to zoom):

import StepViewer from '../../components/StepViewer.astro';

I also asked these two questions:

### Prompt 2

show me how many tokens, compute power and other resources and benchmark stats for you it took to generate the above design keep the answer concise

### Response 2

I don't have access to internal usage telemetry, so I can't give exact token or compute totals.

| Metric | Available information |
|---|---|
| Tokens consumed | Not exposed |
| GPU/CPU time, memory, energy or cost | Not exposed |
| Tools used | Web research, Python, CadQuery/OpenCascade, PDF generation and CAD rendering |
| CAD validation | 119 valid solids; zero detected overlaps; 5 sampled gear positions checked |
| Deliverables | 10-page report, ~11 MB STEP, ~3.1 MB complete ZIP |
| Engineering benchmarks | No FEA, physical testing or measured thermal/endurance results |

### Prompt 3

what are the betterments you can do in the design

### Response 3

The biggest improvement is to **make the design production-ready before increasing torque**. The current model is a preliminary layout.

| Priority | Improvement | Benefit |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | Confirm the actual motor dimensions and winding/lead clearances with CubeMars | Resolves the **28 vs 31.5 mm** discrepancy and prevents assembly clashes. |
| **2** | Replace simplified gear roots with manufacturable fillets; optimize module, pressure angle and tooth counts | Improves the weakest component (the sun gear) and establishes a defensible torque rating. |
| **3** | Run gear-contact and structural FEA, including unequal planet loading and landing shocks | Checks stresses and deflections that the hand calculations cannot establish. |
| **4** | Reduce housing, carrier and rotor-bell mass through load-based pocketing | The current **~2.86 kg** is heavy; reducing rotating mass also improves response. |
| **5** | Finalize bearing fits, preload, pin retention and housing stiffness | Improves alignment, backlash, durability and resistance to joint bending loads. |
| **6** | Validate the aluminium heat sleeve and cooling experimentally | Establishes genuine continuous torque and allowable burst duration. |
| **7** | Add sealing, lubrication provisions, wiring protection and encoder mounts | Makes the actuator practical for a quadruped environment. |
| **8** | Optimize backlash, friction and reflected inertia, then bench-test | Establishes actual backdrivability, efficiency and control performance. |

**My recommended next revision:** resolve motor fit, redesign and rate the gears, then reduce mass. I would **not increase the provisional ~45 N·m output rating** until those checks support it.

### My take

I am pretty sure this design will work if I tuned a few parts myself, like the wiring hole and clearances. After that I just have to 3D print it and it will work.

The only thing I don't like is the thickness of the walls in some parts are either too thick or too thin. I understand it did not perform FEA, but I think at this stage it is not capable of doing that, as it requires a completely god-tier harness. You will also notice most of the design is really simple; it is either a cylinder or a rectangle with intelligent placement. You can also notice it does not have any complicated shapes or features like fillets and chamfers for stress dissipation, which also requires FEA knowledge. But for 35 min 13 sec time to generate, it did a pretty good job. It is pretty insane to see how quickly AI is advancing. I am excited to see what else this design harness can do for people.

Especially for Mech Engineering students, when I was in my 1st/2nd year I was so confused on how to get started with design. I think now you can ask AI to generate a design and explain on what basis it selected a few components, and actually think like a design engineer. I will explain it to you like you are a baby.

It still has a lot to improve.
